BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal. Seller documents treated as the counterparty's untrusted draft and tested against the Buyer Playbook. Nothing below assumes any Playbook fallback has been authorised; I have checked and no Amelia Frost written authority is on file for any fallback.

---

## 1. Threshold observation: the Seller's framing

The Seller letter describes its package as "fair and balanced", several items as "agreed", "addressed", "adequate" or "settled", and the funds flow as reflecting "the agreed price mechanics". Under Playbook sec 0.4/6.3 none of these labels carry weight. On my read, **nothing in this draft has been agreed by us**; each item below is a live negotiation point. The Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) concedes that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included", which undercuts the cover letter's characterisations.

Two points deserve particular care because they superficially resemble our fallbacks:

- **Cap at 20% / AUD 4.8m** – this is exactly our conditional fallback figure. It is *not* cleared merely because the number matches. The fallback requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none exists. Our position remains **25% / AUD 6.0m**.
- **18-month claims period** – same analysis. No approval given. Our position remains **24 months**.

We should assume the Seller may be aware of typical buyer fallbacks and is anchoring at them. We should not reward that by conceding at the outset.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General Warranty cap (Seller cl 12.1) – DEPARTS
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m.
- Playbook: 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with written authority (not given).
- **Push back:** Re-insert 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not trade this early; the cap interacts with the thresholds and the Fundamental/Title regime, so it should be resolved as a package.

### 2.2 Thresholds (Seller cl 12.2) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery (deductible).
- Playbook: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's numbers are 5× ours on each threshold, and the switch from tipping to deductible structure is a substantive economic transfer, not a drafting nuance. On a AUD 24m deal, an AUD 250k deductible plus AUD 25k per-claim exclusion could eliminate most realistic operational warranty claims (e.g. several of the DD items below individually sit in the AUD 100–200k range).
- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket. Confirm expressly that related claims arising from the same facts aggregate for de minimis purposes.

### 2.3 Time limits and "all Claims" limitation (Seller cl 12.3/13) – DEPARTS, with a hidden structural override
- Seller: 18 months; and "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- Playbook: 24 months general; 18 only with written approval (none); separate regimes for Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** The second sentence is the more dangerous one. It is a default rule that sweeps every limitation (cap, basket, time bar, knowledge exclusion, non-reliance) across every category of claim unless we remember to carve each one out. That inverts the Playbook structure and creates the "hidden general-regime override" we are instructed to resist. Combined with 2.4 and 2.5 below, it would collapse Title, Tax, IP, indemnities and fraud into the 20%/18-month box.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence and replace with the reverse default: limitations in cl 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and not to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, completion-payment or covenant claims, or fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: capacity and title subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- Playbook: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason; it is a 20%/18-month limit on our recourse if we do not get good title to the shares we are paying AUD 24m for. This is a non-negotiable for a buyer.
- **Push back:** Separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% cap, 6-year (minimum) claims period, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualification, no disclosure against them.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (Seller cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Playbook: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** "Claims of any nature" on its face includes fraud. Apart from the policy/enforceability questions, this is a position we are not authorised to accept and should not spend negotiating capital on – it is a clean "no".
- **Push back:** Insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out overriding cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. Confirm the exclusive-remedy clause does not exclude specific performance, injunctive relief, or claims under specific indemnities and completion covenants.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- Playbook: specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Para 1.1 is a blanket data-room disclosure; para 1.2 adds public registers. Taken together with cl 8.3 (buyer knowledge, below), these would mean that anything in the data room, however buried, defeats a warranty claim. The specific disclosures in paras 2–10 are actually reasonably candid (they repeatedly state what has *not* been provided) – which is helpful to us and should be preserved – but they are framed as "without limiting" the general disclosure.
- **Push back:** Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: disclosed only to the extent set out in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data room documents may be referred to only where specifically identified against a specific warranty. No disclosure against Fundamental/Title warranties or specific indemnities.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge exclusion (Seller cl 8.3) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- Playbook: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar ("discoverable"), extends to advisers, and has no limits by category. It duplicates and compounds the general-disclosure problem – effectively a second whole-data-room disclosure. It would also arguably bar claims on matters we flagged in DD (e.g. DD-004/005/006) precisely *because* we flagged them.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. Where the Seller wants knowledge qualifiers on *its* warranties, limit to the actual knowledge of named Seller individuals after due enquiry. Expressly state that Buyer knowledge (actual or constructive) does not affect any Claim, with an overriding statement that it cannot excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (Seller cl 3/6.3; DL para 2) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
- Playbook: effective consent **and** evidence its conditions (cl 11.3 of the Bluefen contract) are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient.
- **Facts (per DL para 2, Seller's own admission):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); the consent is subject to conditions in cl 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction has been provided**. The word "addressed" in the cover letter is therefore not supported by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.
- **Reasoning:** A consent-on-delivery mechanism would allow Completion against a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet; if the conditions then fail, our 30% customer may walk and we have no condition protection. "Reasonable endeavours" gives us no remedy if the Seller simply fails.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent: delivery of Bluefen's unconditional written consent **or** written consent together with evidence reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer that every cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied. Seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours" (consider "best endeavours" given materiality), with Buyer involvement in communications. Buyer-only waiver right. Consider a Bluefen revenue-protection mechanism (retention/specific indemnity) if the Seller resists.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (Seller cl 2/7; DL para 3) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
- Playbook: current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval (none given).
- **Facts (DL para 3):** not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; the facility has a change-of-control clause (8.1).
- **Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. Completing with AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt outstanding, a change-of-control trigger, and only a promise of a later release means we would own a company in default on day one with the lender's security still in place. The "approximately" figure is also not a payout figure.
- **Push back:** Require (i) a lender payout letter dated within a few days of Completion, (ii) repayment direct to Riverlark from the purchase price at Completion as part of the funds flow, (iii) executed deeds of release/discharge of all security (including PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion, in escrow if necessary. Only if Amelia Frost approves in writing could we accept an irrevocable lender undertaking to release post-Completion, and even then with the payout funded at Completion.

### 2.10 Funds flow and DD-005 employee bonuses – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised; funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics".
- Playbook: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Facts (DL para 5):** AUD 420k conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Reasoning:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities that crystallise in the Company (our company, post-Completion). "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the SPA actually makes the Seller pay. Silence in the funds flow means the Company bears them. On-costs (super, payroll tax) could add a material percentage to the AUD 420k.
- **Push back:** Either (i) a specific funds-flow line deducting AUD 420,000 plus a calculated on-cost gross-up from the price, or (ii) treating the gross amount as Debt/transaction expenses in the completion accounts, or (iii) a Seller specific indemnity for the gross bonus cost, uncapped and outside the basket. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing before signing. Nothing in the funds flow is "agreed" until this is resolved.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (Seller cl 11.1; DL para 4) – DEPARTS
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate".
- Playbook: broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- **Facts (DL para 4):** cl 7.3 of the Ironquay contract conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's own letter notes DD-010 is "not independent bank verification of non-payment".
- **Reasoning:** The risk is not just the AUD 180k; it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables (and any downstream products built on them) until payment clears. An indemnity for the payment alone does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, or re-development cost if Ironquay disputes or the assignment fails.
- **Push back:** (i) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay; failing which (ii) a broadened specific indemnity covering all loss arising from any defect in title to or right to use the Ironquay Project Materials, including re-development cost and third-party claims, not just the fee. Keep the cure route open (payment + assignment extinguishes the indemnity). Independently verify the AUD 180k via bank records/Ironquay statement – do not accept either DD-010 or the Seller's "not verified" framing as establishing payment status.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident DD-006 (Seller cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6) – DEPARTS in characterisation
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- Playbook: preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Facts (DL para 6):** download link sent to an unintended external email; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation preliminary.
- **Reasoning:** We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion nor over-characterise it. The Seller's own disclosure says the key questions are unanswered. Our concern is process and allocation of unknown risk, not a figure.
- **Push back:** (i) Pre-signing covenant to preserve all logs and evidence and continue the investigation; (ii) written updates and access for the Buyer to the investigation, with a bring-down at Completion; (iii) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), outside the general cap/basket, triggered only if loss materialises; (iv) specific warranty that the disclosure is complete and accurate as at Completion. No price adjustment proposed at this stage and no assumption of a notification duty.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals AUD 330,000 (DL para 8) – ASSESS, no departure yet
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs.
- Playbook: assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Facts:** three related renewals of AUD 110k each (DD-008/DD-011, to be read together for timing/scope); Seller does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller asserts ordinary course; its Disclosure Letter declines to say so. We should not accept the label, but nor should we assume Debt.
- **Push back / action:** Request the three contracts and timing; determine whether any amount is accrued/payable pre-Completion (then completion accounts item) or is a genuine post-Completion operating cost (then no adjustment). Ask the Seller to warrant the characterisation it is asserting.

### 2.14 Tax and IP (Seller: "settled under the general regime") – DEPARTS
- Playbook: terms remain OPEN; keep Tax/IP separate; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Reasoning:** "Settled" is an assertion only. Folding Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month regime (reinforced by the cl 13 "all Claims" default) is a significant concession we have not made and are not authorised to make. Equally, we are not instructed to demand unlimited liability.
- **Push back:** State that Tax and IP positions remain open and are to be negotiated as separate categories with their own cap and period (Tax period typically aligned to the statutory review period). Do not accept the cl 13 default sweeping them in.

### 2.15 Title to shares (DL para 10; Seller "evidenced by DD-012") – DEPARTS
- Seller: share register at DD-012 evidences title.
- Playbook: independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Reasoning:** The register is a Company-generated document supplied by the Seller. The Seller's own para 10 acknowledges it "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification". Note also that Riverlark's security (para 3) may extend to the shares – we have no discharge.
- **Action / push back:** Independent ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (shares and assets), ASIC search of the Seller, board/constitution authority evidence for the Seller, original share certificates and executed transfers at Completion, and Fundamental warranties on title/encumbrances under the 100%/6-year regime. Treat the Riverlark discharge as a title item, not just a debt item.

### 2.16 Lower-priority items from the Disclosure Letter
- **DL para 1.4 (no admissions):** acceptable in principle but must not be read as reducing the scope of specific disclosures or as a knowledge qualifier; we should add that the Disclosure Letter does not limit specific indemnities.
- **Office lease DD-007:** notification obligation, not consent. Require the Seller to give the notification pre-Completion (or covenant to do so jointly) and confirm no consent requirement in writing.
- **Mossvale DD-009:** assignment restriction, not change of control. Confirm by review of the actual clause; warranty that no counterparty consent is triggered by the share sale.

---

## 3. Interaction risk – the "stacking" problem

The most important point for the team is that items 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7 and 2.14 are designed to work together. Individually each looks like a drafting preference; collectively they produce a single 20% / 18-month regime with (i) whole-data-room disclosure, (ii) a constructive buyer-knowledge bar, (iii) no separate title, tax or IP recourse, and (iv) no fraud carve-out. We should respond to them as a structural package, not line by line, and the opening response should restate our architecture (general / Fundamental / Tax / IP / specific indemnities / covenants as separate regimes, fraud outside all of them).

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our response |
|---|------|-----------------|--------------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **Revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m.** Fallback not authorised. |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first-dollar (tipping).** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims by default | **24 months.** Delete "all Claims" default; limits apply only to general Warranty Claims. |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** |
| 5 | Fraud / exclusive remedy / non-reliance | Apply to all Claims | **Express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct.** Non-negotiable. |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | **Delete DL 1.1–1.2; specific fair disclosure only; none against Fundamental warranties or indemnities.** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Blanket, incl. "discoverable" | **Delete.** Seller-knowledge qualifiers only, named persons, reasonable enquiry. |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP: effective consent + evidence cl 11.3 conditions met before Completion.** Stronger endeavours; Buyer-only waiver. |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | **Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion.** Post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. |
| 10 | DD-005 bonuses | Not itemised; "matter for Seller" | **Specific line item incl. on-costs, or seller-funded via indemnity/Debt.** Funds flow not agreed. |
| 11 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 fee | **Broaden to all loss from defective title/use of Project Materials; preserve payment-and-assignment cure; verify AUD 180k independently.** |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Log preservation, investigation, updates, bring-down, specific indemnity if loss arises.** No breach assumed; no number proposed. |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess contracts and timing; no automatic Debt treatment; ask Seller to warrant characterisation.** |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Remain OPEN; separate categories; no unlimited liability demanded.** |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent ASIC/PPSR/authority searches; certificates and transfers at Completion; Riverlark discharge as title item.** |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification / assignment restriction | Confirm by review; notification pre-Completion; warranty no consents triggered. |

**Authority points for Amelia Frost (decision, not recommendation to concede):** the Seller has anchored at our 20% cap and 18-month fallbacks. I recommend we hold 25%/24 months and do not seek fallback authority at this stage; if the team wants the option available for a later trade, a written request to Ms Frost identifying this draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update) would be required before any such concession is signalled.

**Suggested next steps:** (1) issue a mark-up restating our regime architecture and the above positions; (2) commission the independent title/PPSR/ASIC searches and the Ironquay payment verification now; (3) request the Bluefen consent correspondence, Riverlark payout letter, Sandbar contracts and DD-006 investigation log preservation confirmation as immediate information requests; (4) obtain Seller's written position on bonus on-costs for the funds flow.

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal. Seller documents treated as the counterparty's untrusted draft and tested against the Buyer Playbook. Nothing below assumes any Playbook fallback has been authorised; I have checked and no Amelia Frost written authority is on file for any fallback.

## 1. Threshold observation: the Seller's framing

The Seller letter describes its package as "fair and balanced", several items as "agreed", "addressed", "adequate" or "settled", and the funds flow as reflecting "the agreed price mechanics". Under Playbook sec 0.4/6.3 none of these labels carry weight. On my read, **nothing in this draft has been agreed by us**; each item below is a live negotiation point. The Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) concedes that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included", which undercuts the cover letter's characterisations.

Two points deserve particular care because they superficially resemble our fallbacks:

- **Cap at 20% / AUD 4.8m** – this is exactly our conditional fallback figure. It is *not* cleared merely because the number matches. The fallback requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none exists. Our position remains **25% / AUD 6.0m**.
- **18-month claims period** – same analysis. No approval given. Our position remains **24 months**.

We should assume the Seller may be aware of typical buyer fallbacks and is anchoring at them. We should not reward that by conceding at the outset.

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General Warranty cap (Seller cl 12.1) – DEPARTS
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m.
- Playbook: 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% only with written authority (not given).
- **Push back:** Re-insert 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not trade this early; the cap interacts with the thresholds and the Fundamental/Title regime, so it should be resolved as a package.

### 2.2 Thresholds (Seller cl 12.2) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery (deductible).
- Playbook: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's numbers are 5× ours on each threshold, and the switch from tipping to deductible structure is a substantive economic transfer, not a drafting nuance. On a AUD 24m deal, an AUD 250k deductible plus AUD 25k per-claim exclusion could eliminate most realistic operational warranty claims (e.g. several of the DD items below individually sit in the AUD 100–200k range).
- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket. Confirm expressly that related claims arising from the same facts aggregate for de minimis purposes.

### 2.3 Time limits and "all Claims" limitation (Seller cl 12.3/13) – DEPARTS, with a hidden structural override
- Seller: 18 months; and "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- Playbook: 24 months general; 18 only with written approval (none); separate regimes for Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** The second sentence is the more dangerous one. It is a default rule that sweeps every limitation (cap, basket, time bar, knowledge exclusion, non-reliance) across every category of claim unless we remember to carve each one out. That inverts the Playbook structure and creates the "hidden general-regime override" we are instructed to resist. Combined with 2.4 and 2.5 below, it would collapse Title, Tax, IP, indemnities and fraud into the 20%/18-month box.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence and replace with the reverse default: limitations in cl 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and not to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, completion-payment or covenant claims, or fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: capacity and title subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- Playbook: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason; it is a 20%/18-month limit on our recourse if we do not get good title to the shares we are paying AUD 24m for. This is a non-negotiable for a buyer.
- **Push back:** Separate Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% cap, 6-year (minimum) claims period, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualification, no disclosure against them.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (Seller cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Playbook: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** "Claims of any nature" on its face includes fraud. Apart from the policy/enforceability questions, this is a position we are not authorised to accept and should not spend negotiating capital on – it is a clean "no".
- **Push back:** Insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out overriding cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. Confirm the exclusive-remedy clause does not exclude specific performance, injunctive relief, or claims under specific indemnities and completion covenants.

### 2.6 Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- Playbook: specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Para 1.1 is a blanket data-room disclosure; para 1.2 adds public registers. Taken together with cl 8.3 (buyer knowledge, below), these would mean that anything in the data room, however buried, defeats a warranty claim. The specific disclosures in paras 2–10 are actually reasonably candid (they repeatedly state what has *not* been provided) – which is helpful to us and should be preserved – but they are framed as "without limiting" the general disclosure.
- **Push back:** Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: disclosed only to the extent set out in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data room documents may be referred to only where specifically identified against a specific warranty. No disclosure against Fundamental/Title warranties or specific indemnities.

### 2.7 Buyer knowledge exclusion (Seller cl 8.3) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- Playbook: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar ("discoverable"), extends to advisers, and has no limits by category. It duplicates and compounds the general-disclosure problem – effectively a second whole-data-room disclosure. It would also arguably bar claims on matters we flagged in DD (e.g. DD-004/005/006) precisely *because* we flagged them.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. Where the Seller wants knowledge qualifiers on *its* warranties, limit to the actual knowledge of named Seller individuals after due enquiry. Expressly state that Buyer knowledge (actual or constructive) does not affect any Claim, with an overriding statement that it cannot excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent (Seller cl 3/6.3; DL para 2) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
- Playbook: effective consent **and** evidence its conditions (cl 11.3 of the Bluefen contract) are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient.
- **Facts (per DL para 2, Seller's own admission):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); the consent is subject to conditions in cl 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction has been provided**. The word "addressed" in the cover letter is therefore not supported by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.
- **Reasoning:** A consent-on-delivery mechanism would allow Completion against a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet; if the conditions then fail, our 30% customer may walk and we have no condition protection. "Reasonable endeavours" gives us no remedy if the Seller simply fails.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent: delivery of Bluefen's unconditional written consent **or** written consent together with evidence reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer that every cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied. Seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours" (consider "best endeavours" given materiality), with Buyer involvement in communications. Buyer-only waiver right. Consider a Bluefen revenue-protection mechanism (retention/specific indemnity) if the Seller resists.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility (Seller cl 2/7; DL para 3) – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
- Playbook: current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval (none given).
- **Facts (DL para 3):** not repaid; no final discharge of security in the data room; the facility has a change-of-control clause (8.1).
- **Reasoning:** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal. Completing with AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt outstanding, a change-of-control trigger, and only a promise of a later release means we would own a company in default on day one with the lender's security still in place. The "approximately" figure is also not a payout figure.
- **Push back:** Require (i) a lender payout letter dated within a few days of Completion, (ii) repayment direct to Riverlark from the purchase price at Completion as part of the funds flow, (iii) executed deeds of release/discharge of all security (including PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion, in escrow if necessary. Only if Amelia Frost approves in writing could we accept an irrevocable lender undertaking to release post-Completion, and even then with the payout funded at Completion.

### 2.10 Funds flow and DD-005 employee bonuses – MATERIAL DEPARTURE
- Seller: bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised; funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics".
- Playbook: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Facts (DL para 5):** AUD 420k conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Reasoning:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities that crystallise in the Company (our company, post-Completion). "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the SPA actually makes the Seller pay. Silence in the funds flow means the Company bears them. On-costs (super, payroll tax) could add a material percentage to the AUD 420k.
- **Push back:** Either (i) a specific funds-flow line deducting AUD 420,000 plus a calculated on-cost gross-up from the price, or (ii) treating the gross amount as Debt/transaction expenses in the completion accounts, or (iii) a Seller specific indemnity for the gross bonus cost, uncapped and outside the basket. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing before signing. Nothing in the funds flow is "agreed" until this is resolved.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP (Seller cl 11.1; DL para 4) – DEPARTS
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate".
- Playbook: broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- **Facts (DL para 4):** cl 7.3 of the Ironquay contract conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's own letter notes DD-010 is "not independent bank verification of non-payment".
- **Reasoning:** The risk is not just the AUD 180k; it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables (and any downstream products built on them) until payment clears. An indemnity for the payment alone does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, or re-development cost if Ironquay disputes or the assignment fails.
- **Push back:** (i) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay; failing which (ii) a broadened specific indemnity covering all loss arising from any defect in title to or right to use the Ironquay Project Materials, including re-development cost and third-party claims, not just the fee. Keep the cure route open (payment + assignment extinguishes the indemnity). Independently verify the AUD 180k via bank records/Ironquay statement – do not accept either DD-010 or the Seller's "not verified" framing as establishing payment status.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident DD-006 (Seller cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6) – DEPARTS in characterisation
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- Playbook: preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Facts (DL para 6):** download link sent to an unintended external email; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation preliminary.
- **Reasoning:** We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" conclusion nor over-characterise it. The Seller's own disclosure says the key questions are unanswered. Our concern is process and allocation of unknown risk, not a figure.
- **Push back:** (i) Pre-signing covenant to preserve all logs and evidence and continue the investigation; (ii) written updates and access for the Buyer to the investigation, with a bring-down at Completion; (iii) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), outside the general cap/basket, triggered only if loss materialises; (iv) specific warranty that the disclosure is complete and accurate as at Completion. No price adjustment proposed at this stage and no assumption of a notification duty.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals AUD 330,000 (DL para 8) – ASSESS, no departure yet
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs.
- Playbook: assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Facts:** three related renewals of AUD 110k each (DD-008/DD-011, to be read together for timing/scope); Seller does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller asserts ordinary course; its Disclosure Letter declines to say so. We should not accept the label, but nor should we assume Debt.
- **Push back / action:** Request the three contracts and timing; determine whether any amount is accrued/payable pre-Completion (then completion accounts item) or is a genuine post-Completion operating cost (then no adjustment). Ask the Seller to warrant the characterisation it is asserting.

### 2.14 Tax and IP (Seller: "settled under the general regime") – DEPARTS
- Playbook: terms remain OPEN; keep Tax/IP separate; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Reasoning:** "Settled" is an assertion only. Folding Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month regime (reinforced by the cl 13 "all Claims" default) is a significant concession we have not made and are not authorised to make. Equally, we are not instructed to demand unlimited liability.
- **Push back:** State that Tax and IP positions remain open and are to be negotiated as separate categories with their own cap and period (Tax period typically aligned to the statutory review period). Do not accept the cl 13 default sweeping them in.

### 2.15 Title to shares (DL para 10; Seller "evidenced by DD-012") – DEPARTS
- Seller: share register at DD-012 evidences title.
- Playbook: independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Reasoning:** The register is a Company-generated document supplied by the Seller. The Seller's own para 10 acknowledges it "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification". Note also that Riverlark's security (para 3) may extend to the shares – we have no discharge.
- **Action / push back:** Independent ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (shares and assets), ASIC search of the Seller, board/constitution authority evidence for the Seller, original share certificates and executed transfers at Completion, and Fundamental warranties on title/encumbrances under the 100%/6-year regime. Treat the Riverlark discharge as a title item, not just a debt item.

### 2.16 Lower-priority items from the Disclosure Letter
- **DL para 1.4 (no admissions):** acceptable in principle but must not be read as reducing the scope of specific disclosures or as a knowledge qualifier; we should add that the Disclosure Letter does not limit specific indemnities.
- **Office lease DD-007:** notification obligation, not consent. Require the Seller to give the notification pre-Completion (or covenant to do so jointly) and confirm no consent requirement in writing.
- **Mossvale DD-009:** assignment restriction, not change of control. Confirm by review of the actual clause; warranty that no counterparty consent is triggered by the share sale.

## 3. Interaction risk – the "stacking" problem

The most important point for the team is that items 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7 and 2.14 are designed to work together. Individually each looks like a drafting preference; collectively they produce a single 20% / 18-month regime with (i) whole-data-room disclosure, (ii) a constructive buyer-knowledge bar, (iii) no separate title, tax or IP recourse, and (iv) no fraud carve-out. We should respond to them as a structural package, not line by line, and the opening response should restate our architecture (general / Fundamental / Tax / IP / specific indemnities / covenants as separate regimes, fraud outside all of them).
